subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` gain OpenClaw skill-context injection, and if so which selection modes, prompt layer, redaction rules, audit metadata, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The capability gap is source-proven, but the change would alter the ACP spawn API, external harness prompt authority, local skill privacy boundary, and Codex-native skill interaction, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design explicit opt-in contract first
options.body: Specify explicit skill ids, prompt layer, redaction/audit fields, token limits, resume behavior, and Codex/ACP compatibility before implementation.

options.title: Limit first pass to explicit skill ids
options.body: Allow only per-call `skills: [...]` injection initially and defer `auto` and default sets until observability and security behavior are proven.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Keep ACP harnesses isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skills and direct users to harness-native skills, MCP bridges, or plugin workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Design explicit opt-in contract first
recommendation.body: Specify explicit skill ids, prompt layer, redaction/audit fields, token limits, resume behavior, and Codex/ACP compatibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP runtime/session boundary and are the strongest routing candidate for the API and security-boundary decision.
